t.4.58.1: Then, having heard those words, sweet as the taste of nectar, spoken by the king of vultures as he spoke, those bulls among the monkeys were delighted.
t.4.58.2: Then Jāmbavān, the best of the monkeys, together with all the monkeys, rose suddenly from the ground and spoke to the king of vultures.
t.4.58.3: Where is Sītā? By whom has she been seen, and who is carrying off Maithilī? Let your honor tell all of that; be the refuge of the forest-dwellers.
t.4.58.5: Pleased, he once more reassured the monkeys, who were filled with joy and intent on hearing news of Sītā, and spoke these words.
t.4.58.4: Who does not reflect upon the might of Dāśarathi's arrows, which fall with the force of a thunderbolt, and of those said to belong to Lakṣmaṇa himself?
t.4.58.6: Hear now how I came to learn of the abduction of Vaidehī, who it was that told me of it, and where the long-eyed lady now is.
t.4.58.7: Old as I am, with my vital strength and prowess wasted away, I have long since fallen upon this inaccessible mountain, which stretches for many yojanas.
t.4.58.8: My son, Supārśva by name, the best of birds, sustains me, who am in such a state, with food at the proper times.
t.4.58.9: The Gandharvas are intense in desire, and serpents are intense in wrath; the fear of deer is intense, and we, in turn, are intense in hunger.
t.4.58.10: Once, when I was tormented by hunger and longing for food, my son came to me at the close of the day, after the sun had set, without any meat.
t.4.58.11: Overcome by hunger and thirst, I, out of my old age and out of anger, harshly rebuked that youth, the best of birds.
t.4.58.12: He, the increaser of my joy, distressed because my food had been held back, conciliated me and spoke these words, telling things just as they truly were.
t.4.58.13: Father, at the proper time, seeking food, I flew up into the sky and took my position, blocking the pass of the mountain Mahendra.
t.4.58.14: There I stayed alone, with my face turned downward, in order to block the path of the thousands of creatures that move within the ocean.
t.4.58.15: There I saw someone who resembled a heap of crushed collyrium, going along carrying off a woman whose radiance was like the rising of the sun.
t.4.58.17: Indeed, nowhere is there anyone, even among the lowest of men, who would strike those who approach with conciliation; how much less, alas, one such as I!
t.4.58.16: Seeing those two, I, wanting food, made up my mind to seize them; but with that humble and conciliatory speech I was entreated to give way.
t.4.58.18: He departed through the sky with splendour, as though contracting it by his speed; then I was approached and honoured by the beings that range the sky.
t.4.58.19: The great sages said to me, "By good fortune you are alive, dear one! Somehow that one has gone away with his woman; without doubt all is well with you."
t.4.58.20: Thus addressed then by those most splendid Siddhas, I was also told that he was Rāvaṇa, the king of the Rākṣasas.
t.4.58.21: He was carrying off the daughter of Janaka, the wife of Rāma, son of Daśaratha, her ornaments and silken garment slipping away, overcome by the force of her grief.
t.4.58.23: Supārśva reported this whole matter to me. Yet even after hearing it, I had no thought whatsoever of valorous action.
t.4.58.22: I saw her crying out the names of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, her hair hanging loose. "Such is the time that has passed since then," said that foremost of those skilled in speech.
t.4.58.24: For how could a bird without wings undertake any task at all? Yet there is still that which can be done by me, who abide in the powers of speech and understanding.
t.4.58.26: You, sirs, are foremost in wisdom, mighty and resolute; united with the king of the monkeys, you are hard to assail even for the gods.
t.4.58.25: Listen, I shall tell you that which depends on your valor; with word and thought I shall do what is pleasing to all of you, for whatever is the task of Dāśarathi is mine as well, there is no doubt of this.
t.4.58.27: And the sharp arrows of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, fletched with heron feathers, are capable of both protecting and subduing even the three worlds.
t.4.58.28: Granted, the ten-headed Daśagrīva is endowed with splendour and strength; but for capable ones such as you, nothing whatsoever is too difficult.
t.4.58.29: So enough of this delay; let a firm decision be made. For wise ones such as you do not linger over their undertakings.
